data.title: Establish required data expectations for new mappings
data.when: A task involves adding or modifying a data mapping, but runtime errors occur that suggest the system is running under incorrect assumptions about the input state or necessary preconditions.
procedure: Identify all implicit assumptions made by the new mapping logic (e.g., required fields must exist, specific states must be true).
Implement an explicit setup phase to meet these identified expectations (e.g., mocking data structures, setting default configuration values, or initializing necessary related entities).
Run a smoke test specifically designed to validate the prerequisite state before executing the core mapping addition/amend process.
pitfalls: Ignoring initial runtime failures and proceeding with the main task logic, leading to `NullPointerExceptions` or validation failures that point to missing preconditions.
Assuming existing documentation covers necessary state setup when a new field requires an explicit default value in testing/run time.
verification: The test run passes successfully after the dedicated prerequisite setup phase is completed, indicating the system accepted the mapping without unexpected exceptions regarding data state or context.
